subject.title: feat(channels): add typed cross-surface approval actions

question: Should an otherwise authorized resolution carrying the wrong explicit approval kind terminally deny the canonical pending approval as malformed, or return not-found without mutation?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible security policies: terminal denial fails closed against tampering, while no mutation avoids stale or misbound controls cancelling legitimate work; repository source cannot establish the permanent product and security intent.

options.title: Keep terminal fail-closed denial
options.body: Accept the current behavior, document it as the canonical security contract, and require live proof that channels cannot accidentally produce mismatched owner kinds.

options.title: Reject without mutation
options.body: Change wrong-kind resolutions to an approval-not-found response so stale or misbound callbacks cannot terminate the real pending record.

recommendation.title: Keep terminal fail-closed denial
recommendation.body: Accept the current behavior, document it as the canonical security contract, and require live proof that channels cannot accidentally produce mismatched owner kinds.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the current durable-approvals design and the adjacent merged approval authorization work.
